Package neqsim.process.mechanicaldesign.valve.choke

Class ChokeOperatingEnvelope

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.mechanicaldesign.valve.choke.ChokeOperatingEnvelope
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class ChokeOperatingEnvelope extends Object implements Serializable
Screening of a production choke against recommended sizing and operating limits.

The checks cover the points that decide whether a choke is acceptable in service:

  • Operating range: operate above about 20 % of maximum Cv for plug-and-cage trims and above about 60 % for rotating-disc trims. A minimum position calculated from throttling velocity, pressure drop and sand load replaces the 20 % default for plug-and-cage trims when it is supplied; without a calculation, keep at least 20 % of maximum Cv in sand service.
  • Clean-up: the smallest port in the trim should be at least three times the largest particle expected.
  • Collapse capacity: the pressure-protection system must be able to handle the flow of a collapsed (fully open) choke. Supply the collapsed flow, for example from the choke model with the maximum Cv, and the protection capacity.
  • Noise: optional comparison of a predicted level with a limit.
  • Opening speed: the choke should open more slowly than the upstream block valve.

The limits are screening recommendations. A WARN is a deviation that needs an explicit justification; a FAIL is a violated hard criterion. Checks without input are reported as NOT_EVALUATED and never count as a pass.
